image.alt: ASUS Makes TIME’s World’s Best Companies 2026 List for the Third Time

children: today announced its third appearance in TIME’s esteemed list of the World’s Best Companies. This accolade recognizes organizations that set the standard in employee satisfaction, revenue growth, and sustainability transparency. The inclusion highlights ASUS’s commitment to excellence in the IT, Electronics, Hardware, and Equipment industry, with a constant focus on people, innovation, and sustainability.

TIME’s World’s Best Companies 2026 ranking offers valuable insight into what defines corporate success today — guiding consumers, investors, and policymakers to support the world’s most forward-thinking businesses.
“We are honored that ASUS has again been recognized by TIME as one of the World’s Best Companies,” said S.Y. Hsu, ASUS Co-CEO. “This reflects the progress of our

strategy as we build a comprehensive AI ecosystem — from infrastructure and accelerators to AI PCs, edge applications, and real-world solutions. By uniting our innovation capabilities across the company, ASUS is turning AI into meaningful experiences that create value for customers, industries, and society.”

“We are proud to receive this recognition from TIME, which underscores our commitment to sustainable growth and responsible innovation,” said Samson Hu, ASUS Co-CEO. “Through stronger sustainability governance and initiatives such as our AI x ESG Platform, ASUS is making sustainability data more transparent, proactive, and actionable. As we advance toward our 2050 net-zero goal, we remain focused on creating long-term value for people, partners, and the planet.”

In Canada, the recognition follows a year of expansion for the local team, including the appointment of Vernon Coutinho as Country Manager in May. "We've built real momentum in Canada, and it comes down to the team here," said Shawn Chang, General Manager, ASUS North America System Business Group. "Being ranked by TIME on employee satisfaction as well as growth and sustainability tells us we're building the business the right way, and we'll keep investing in Canadian talent to do it."

ASUS continues to drive innovation and excellence in technology, earning global recognition for its commitment to enhancing lives and delivering incredible experiences. The company was recently recognized on
for the 11th time, listed on Forbes’ 2026 America’s Best Employers for Company Culture, and it topped Interbrand’s 2025 Best Taiwan Global Brands for the 12th time.

The revenue growth TIME recognized comes from a portfolio that runs from AI infrastructure to the devices people use every day, including Zenbook, Vivobook and ProArt AI PCs, ExpertBook commercial laptops and ROG gaming hardware. With more additions like the NVIDIA RTX Spark-powered ProArt P16 and ProArt P14 showcased this month at IFA 2026.

TIME's World's Best Companies 2026 list, compiled with Statista, ranks 1,000 companies on three equally weighted dimensions: employee satisfaction, based on surveys of more than 200,000 employees worldwide; revenue growth over the past three years, both relative and absolute; and sustainability transparency, based on standardized ESG metrics such as carbon emissions intensity, CDP scores and the quality of ESG reporting.

ASUS (2357.TW) is an innovative technology leader delivering the world’s most comprehensive AI solutions across Infrastructure, Physical AI, AI PC/Devices, and Engineering the AI Advantage. Guided by its “Ubiquitous AI. Incredible Possibilities” strategy, ASUS is bringing enterprise-to-edge AI to life. The ASUS portfolio also includes the ROG and ProArt sub-brands, which serve gamers and creators worldwide.
